hints: Convert the equation to one variable by writing both cotangents in terms of $t=\tan\theta$.
Solve for both tangent values, then find every corresponding angle in $0^\circ<\theta<180^\circ$.
walkthrough:
Rewrite the cotangent terms in the equation $\cot\theta - \cot(\theta + 45^\circ) = 3$ using $\cot A = \dfrac{1}{\tan A}$:
$$\dfrac{1}{\tan\theta} - \dfrac{1}{\tan(\theta + 45^\circ)} = 3$$

Apply the tangent addition formula $\tan(\theta + 45^\circ) = \dfrac{\tan\theta + \tan 45^\circ}{1 - \tan\theta\tan 45^\circ}$:
Since $\tan 45^\circ = 1$:
$$\tan(\theta + 45^\circ) = \dfrac{\tan\theta + 1}{1 - \tan\theta}$$
Therefore:
$$\dfrac{1}{\tan(\theta + 45^\circ)} = \dfrac{1 - \tan\theta}{1 + \tan\theta}$$

Substitute this reciprocal into the equation (letting $t = \tan\theta$ for simplicity):
$$\dfrac{1}{t} - \dfrac{1 - t}{1 + t} = 3$$

Combine the left-hand side fractions over the common denominator $t(1 + t)$:
$$\dfrac{(1 + t) - t(1 - t)}{t(1 + t)} = 3$$
$$\dfrac{1 + t - t + t^2}{t + t^2} = 3$$
$$\dfrac{1 + t^2}{t + t^2} = 3$$

Multiply both sides by $(t + t^2)$:
$$1 + t^2 = 3(t + t^2) = 3t + 3t^2$$

Collect all terms to form a standard quadratic equation:
$$3t^2 - t^2 + 3t - 1 = 0$$
$$2t^2 + 3t - 1 = 0 \quad \left(\text{or } 2\tan^2\theta + 3\tan\theta - 1 = 0\right)$$

Solve the quadratic equation for $t = \tan\theta$ using the quadratic formula:
$$\tan\theta = \dfrac{-3 \pm \sqrt{3^2 - 4(2)(-1)}}{2(2)} = \dfrac{-3 \pm \sqrt{9 + 8}}{4} = \dfrac{-3 \pm \sqrt{17}}{4}$$

Calculate the two possible values of $\tan\theta$:
$$\tan\theta_1 = \dfrac{-3 + \sqrt{17}}{4} \approx \dfrac{-3 + 4.123106}{4} = \dfrac{1.123106}{4} \approx 0.280776$$
$$\tan\theta_2 = \dfrac{-3 - \sqrt{17}}{4} \approx \dfrac{-3 - 4.123106}{4} = \dfrac{-7.123106}{4} \approx -1.780776$$

Find the solutions for $\theta$ in the interval $0^\circ < \theta < 180^\circ$:
- For $\tan\theta_1 \approx 0.280776$ (Quadrant I):
$$\theta_1 = \tan^{-1}(0.280776) \approx 15.683^\circ \approx 15.7^\circ$$
- For $\tan\theta_2 \approx -1.780776$ (Quadrant II):
$$\theta_2 = 180^\circ - \tan^{-1}(1.780776) \approx 180^\circ - 60.683^\circ = 119.317^\circ \approx 119.3^\circ$$

State both solutions rounded to 1 decimal place:
$$\theta = 15.7^\circ, \quad 119.3^\circ$$
